content.intro: This lesson develops topic 158 of the supplied curriculum: **Working with Sets of Numeric Values**. The main starting point is **- Unique values**. content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Treat **Working with Sets of Numeric Values** as an explicit step in an array workflow. This lesson centers on **- Unique values** and the source syllabus's related subtopics. Before trusting a result, identify the input shape and dtype, perform the smallest useful operation, and inspect the output. The example uses synthetic data so you can change one value and observe what changes.

content_blocks.code:
import numpy as np

left = np.array([1, 2, 3]); right = np.array([3, 4, 5])
print(np.setdiff1d(left, right).tolist())

common_mistakes.problem: Assuming object/string/date data behave like floats
common_mistakes.why: Different dtypes provide different operations and semantics.
common_mistakes.fix: Inspect dtype and select matching routines.

common_mistakes.problem: Treating masked values as automatically removed everywhere
common_mistakes.why: Masked-array behavior depends on the operation and conversion boundary.
common_mistakes.fix: Check how downstream libraries treat masks and missing values.
